overreach: The Anritsu comparison page states that R&S battle-card claims should not be used in customer documents without Anritsu official data and third-party evidence
The Keysight battle card notes that its claims about Keysight portfolio, architecture, software, support, Wi‑Fi, RedCap and FR3/6G lack Keysight official datasheets or versioned documentation
The amarisoft comparison table states that multiple claims lack third-party or amarisoft official documentation
Conformance / certification evidence when claiming operator acceptance, PTCRB, GCF or pre-conformance advantages
Internal RF/RRM and GCF/PTCRB updates are not official GCF/PTCRB/CTIA minutes or validation reports
Claims about FR1/FR2/FR3 bandwidth, data rate, fading, IP throughput, Wi‑Fi integration or 'one-box' capability need formal datasheets, option-code mapping, throughput profiles and test conditions
Anritsu 'fragmented tools' positioning can remain R&S sales positioning, but Anritsu’s own brochure supports that MX844030PC uses a common RTD GUI
Internal O-RU competitor, price-point, market-share and test-coverage comparisons require official competitor datasheets, solution briefs, market reports, quotes, contracts or release notes
Sales statements such as fewer calibrations, fewer licenses, lower TCO and higher throughput are not supported by a TCO calculation

Competitor support or warranty claims require official service terms, since KeysightCare claims lack cited service-term documents and Anritsu support claims lack Anritsu official or third-party sources
